messages:
leah: Hey - after upgrading the Python SDK I started getting ModuleNotFoundError when importing the client in VSCode. I ran `pip install redwood-sdk==0.18.0` and it says installed, but `python -c "import redwood"` fails with:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood.client'
```
I feel like this is an env issue but not sure how to repro for you. Using macOS, pyenv + poetry venv.

jess-support: Thanks for the report — can you paste the output of `which python && which pip` and `python -m pip show redwood-sdk`? Also `ls` of the project root if you can.

leah: Sure:
```
$ which python
/Users/leah/.pyenv/shims/python
$ which pip
/Users/leah/.pyenv/shims/pip
$ python -m pip show redwood-sdk
Name: redwood-sdk
Version: 0.18.0
Location: /Users/leah/.local/lib/python3.11/site-packages
```
Project root listing: `app.py`, `requirements.txt`, `redwood.py`, `venv/`

samir: Ah — quick red flag: you have a file named `redwood.py` in your project root. That will shadow the installed package when doing `import redwood`. Can you try `python -c "import importlib; print(importlib.util.find_spec('redwood'))"` to see where Python resolves the module from?

leah: Ran that: `ModuleSpec(name='redwood', loader=<_frozen_importlib_external.SourceFileLoader object at 0x...>, origin='/Users/leah/work/myproj/redwood.py')`

maya-eng: Yep, that's the culprit. When Python imports, local files in the current working directory come first on sys.path. VSCode often runs with workspace root as CWD, so it finds your `redwood.py` instead of the package. If your local file doesn't define `client`, `import redwood.client` will fail.

leah: Ohhh. I thought it was the package. I renamed my file to `redwood_config.py` and restarted the VSCode Python interpreter. Still seeing error for a sec.

pip-bot: Suggestion: ensure you restart the language server/REPL or fully reload VSCode after renaming. Also verify `python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)"` now points to site-packages.

leah: Did that and now:
```
$ python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)"
/Users/leah/.local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py
```
`import redwood.client` works now. Thanks!

jess-support: Great — leaving notes for KB: common gotchas: local module name shadowing, VSCode interpreter mismatch (pyenv/shims), and `pip` vs `python -m pip`. Recommended triage steps we gave: check `which python`, `pip show`, `importlib.util.find_spec`, and inspect repo for conflicting filenames.

samir: Also added a short repro snippet for support docs so we can send a checklist to customers who hit similar errors. Example command to demonstrate shadowing:
```
mkdir repro && cd repro
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install redwood-sdk
# create redwood.py (empty)
python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)"  # shows ./redwood.py instead of site-packages
```

leah: Filing: this was fixed by renaming file and reloading VSCode. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

jess-support: Marking thread resolved — will attach repro to the internal KB entry (support/infra).
